_comment: The CatHarness declaration for THIS instance — what directories it scans and what kind of graph each holds. See skills/folio-core/directory-conventions.md. This repo is PRE-SPLIT (issue #223), so it declares what is true today, not the target layout: `tools/` and `folio/` do not exist here yet and are deliberately not declared. A directory that is declared but absent is worse than one that is missing, because every consumer then scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. NOTE: `schemas/` declares TWO graphs — the first real use of the array. A directory is a place to look and may hold more than one part of the graph; it does not say how to tell them apart, because the files declare what they are (see bean xxxb: schemas/*.ts does not yet do this well). `beans/` is declared ONCE, as a single `beans` graph. Its internal split — `defs` for work items, `workflows` for running BPMN state — is declared by `beans/beans.json`, not here. #263 declared the two as separate directories, one nested inside the other, which left a consumer unable to tell which owned what beneath it; the nodes now carry that.
_title: No `title`, deliberately: `displayTitle` is title || name || id, so the sidebar and the landing page fall back to `name` — which the schema already requires to be the instance's identifier, the one artefacts are stub-named after. A title here said `c@t-harness` and overrode that, labelling THIS repository with the brand of the harness layer that is still to be split out of it. Setting the title to `folio-assistant` instead would be the same fact in two fields, free to drift. The c@t-harness derivation stays in the description, where it is a tagline rather than an identity.

assets.title: AGENTS.md — folio-assistant
assets.description: The file every cold agent reads first, and until 2026-09-19 the ONLY root artefact this instance did not declare — `directories[]` and `images[]` carried everything else. Bean `v8gh` is what that cost: seven dead links, five broken by one directory move, including the one its own banner calls the place to start, so an agent following the banner hit a 404. Nothing caught them; `readme:audit` checks README.md alone and `check:agents-xref` checks citations INTO this file rather than links out of it. `source` names the bootstrap instance it descends from, so "is this still what it was copied from" is a question that can be ASKED — 'it was copied at init' is not an answer.

assets.title: folio-assistant
assets.description: The reader-facing entry point. Its generated sections are written by `readme:sync` only where the file already carries their markers, and `readme:audit` verifies every other link.

assets.title: Initializing into folio-assistant
assets.description: What bootstrap's step 2 reads once it has been pointed at THIS instance. Published at the fixed convention every cat-harness instance honours, composed by `initializationDoc()` rather than spelled, so bootstrap needs no per-target knowledge and can initialise into a SPECIALISED harness it was never written against. Declared as an asset as well as conventional, so `check:declared-assets` verifies it is there and that its links resolve: a convention nothing checks is a convention that is honoured until it quietly is not. The path is INSTANCE-relative here, not `<stub>/docs/...`: this instance has its own directory (`cat-harness/`), so `siteDir` is plain `docs`, and the stub names published artefacts rather than a directory. Whether bootstrap can still find it from one reference is open — see bean `wggr`.

_publication_comment: The `publication host` axis of docs/proposals/deployment-topologies.md, accepted 2026-09-19 (issue #363). WHAT KIND of host serves the renderings — distinct from `canonicalUrl` (the base @ids are minted against) and from `readme.linkStyle` in harness.config.json (how a link to a published artefact is written). This instance really does publish to GitHub Pages, so it declares so; an instance that has not said is `undefined`, which is a third state and must never be read as `github-pages`.

stickies._comment: THE DESCRIPTION, and it comes first: a reader needs to know what this instance IS before an orientation paragraph about the graph's shape means anything. `bodyFrom: description` rather than a copy of it, so the landing page cannot drift from the declaration one line above. The ENGINEER theme, not the plain cat — the owner: "thats what the themne of the current landing page sticky should be, the engineer".

The owner's words are kept VERBATIM, down to the shape of the sentence. It is a joke that carries real information — a gloss on "computable adjudication and agentic test harness", arrived at by way of caaat-harness, ca&at-harness, .c&at-harness, c@t-harness. Sanding it into a product sentence would lose the only part that tells a reader the name is a pun. Plain grumpy cat, NOT the engineer: the owner called this one "plain old grumpy cat", and the two themes differing is the point. The link is ABSOLUTE and points at the source: cat-harness is still to be split out of this repository (issue #223) and has no site of its own, and this instance's canonicalUrl is THIS site — a sticky on the landing page linking to the landing page is a link to itself.
stickies.summary: Please be introduced to a cat
stickies.body: Please be introduced to a cat who acquires things, for whatever purpose — maybe somebody knows.

stickies._comment: Two sentences, not three, because that is what was asked for. Three of the four named map onto a declared graph kind — `folio` is content, `tools` is tools, `cat-harness` is skills — and ACQUISITION DOES NOT. The text is careful not to imply it does: what exists is `uploads/` and `library/`. `readDeclaration` throws on an unknown kind, so prose naming a fifth one would send the next agent looking for something the registry would reject. NO LINKS, deliberately: the four are graph kinds rather than pages, there is no single URL for "tools" to point at, and inventing four would be four more link-shaped values for bean blv9 to collect.
stickies.body:
**Content** is what somebody authors and a reader reads; **acquisition** is how
unstructured and semi-structured sources — documents, data, loose information —
get into the graph in the first place; **tools** are what an agent can call; and
**skills** are the instructions for doing the work.

All four are **declared directories** rather than conventions, so an instance
says which of them it holds and a consumer reads that declaration instead of
walking the tree.

directories.description: Tool definitions, one subdirectory per contributing instance (tools/<stub>/) so a composed instance adds its own without colliding on a filename. tools/index.ts merges them and is the only path a consumer imports. Authored as .ts calling defineTool so a malformed node fails at tsc; the JSON-LD and JSON Schema renderings are generated.

The content-object model and the per-skill JSON Schemas. Declares BOTH graphs: the schema definitions themselves, and `kg` because a schema IS a knowledge-graph node — the .ts files are part of the KG, not a separate island beside it.

The bootstrap graph's SKILLS — what an agent reads before it knows whether this repository is an instance, what kind, or what for. A SECOND `cat-harness` directory beside `skills/`, and the first real use of the topical layout the declaration was built for: `kgRoots()` returns two, and every consumer reading the declaration rather than the literal `skills/` finds both with no code change. IT POINTS AT `bootstrap/skills/`, NOT `bootstrap/`, and the one level matters. `isSkillMd` is declaration-over-location: a markdown file that does not declare `$schema:` IS a skill. `bootstrap/README.md` and `bootstrap/AGENTS.md` declare neither, and they are the bootstrap instance's two DECLARED ASSETS — so a graph rooted at `bootstrap/` counts them as skill nodes and the scan contradicts a declaration that has already answered the question. Measured on this branch before the fix: `skill/AGENTS` was in the export. #422 found this from the other side and declared `skills/` inside `bootstrap/harness.json`; this entry is the same fact at the root, and it is stated twice BY DECISION (2026-09-20) rather than by necessity. THE EARLIER NOTE HERE WAS WRONG and the correction is the useful part: it said "this instance depends on bootstrap" is not expressible because `HarnessConfigDependenciesSchema` knows only `folioAssistant`. That key does not mean the folio-assistant PACKAGE — its own doc comment reads "Other folio-assistant instances this folio depends on", and bootstrap is such an instance by every test the code applies. MEASURED, not argued: writing `cat-harness/harness.config.json` with `{name: "bootstrap", path: "../bootstrap", provides: ["skills"]}` serves bootstrap through `LOCAL_PACKAGES` with `folio-assistant` unmoved. The zod schema needs no change at all. WHAT ACTUALLY BLOCKS IT is one directory entry, and it is not in the dependency schema: bootstrap declares `workflows/` with no `scope`, so cat-harness INHERITS it, and `materialiseDirectories` resolves an inherited path against the INHERITING instance by design — it wants `cat-harness/workflows/`, which does not exist, and `harness:dirs:check` reports `21 declared, 1 missing` and exits 1. The gap it exposes is general and this entry is only where it surfaced: a `ContentDirectory` cannot say whether it is a LAYOUT dependents should reproduce (`uploads/`, `library/`, `voices/`) or merely WHERE ITS OWN CONTENT LIVES (`workflows/`, `schemas/`, `tools/`). Simulated on a fresh folio depending on this instance, `init-folio` would create five directories it has no use for, each with a committed keep-marker — the `dh4f` shape, shipped downstream. Adding that distinction was considered and DECLINED for now: it is a schema change whose per-directory classification is a judgement about every directory here, not a bootstrap workaround. So THIS entry stays, and the thing to fix before deleting it is the convention/content distinction — not the dependency schema. The earlier note here said `resolveSkillDirs` had no caller: it has one — `discoverLocalPackages` — and the reachability it was waiting on arrived with the `scope` fix in `ownDirectories`, which until then resolved this path against the INSTANCE and so dropped it for not existing. REPOSITORY-scoped: it sits at the top of the checkout, not inside this instance, and it is deliberately never overlaid by a dependency.

The knowledge graph. Skill packages, and the four other node kinds that point at them: `roles/roles.json` (a role IS a BPMN swimlane, and carries the skills its lane's activities need), `workflows/*.bpmn` + `workflows/decisions/*.dmn` (the processes those roles act in, reached through the skill that describes them), `requirements/*.json` (conformance obligations whose `satisfiedBy` names the skill or capability discharging them), `permissions/permissions.json` (what an actor may DO in any lane, as opposed to what its lane's role knows), Its audit verdicts are NOT here: they moved to the `qa` tree on 2026-09-19, because a verdict is a QA reviewer's output and placement follows provenance. Note the id is `kg` while the path is `skills/` — ids are stable across a relocation, paths are not.

CRDM as its OWN topical subgraph — its skills and its eight diagrams together, rather than three skills in folio-core and eight .bpmn in skills/workflows/ with nothing but a filename prefix relating them. Owner, 2026-09-20: CRDM, RACI, SDLC and MADR all live under `methodologies/`, each its own subgraph. I proposed a separate `workflow-methodologies/` on the reading that PROCESS methods (how a process runs) and JUDGEMENT methods (how to decide — Kepner-Tregoe, MADR, DMN) are different axes; the owner settled it as ONE tree, which is the better answer for the reason this repository keeps relearning: two directories whose boundary needs a paragraph to explain are two answers to `where do methodologies live`, and the next author picks the wrong one. This is the layout `skillMdDirs` was built for: its own comment names `crdm` as the example of a topical directory that should cost a declaration line and no code change, and `bootstrap/skills/` was the first such root. Each methodology is declared SEPARATELY rather than declaring the parent, because `workflowDirs` resolves `<kgdir>/workflows` — declaring only the parent would leave every diagram undiscovered. SDLC and RACI are deliberately NOT declared until they have content: a declared-but-absent directory is the `dh4f` defect.

Judgement methodologies the harness owns, one sub-graph each: Kepner-Tregoe for a decision, MADR for its record, DMN for the computable case. PARALLEL rather than composable — which applies is contextual, and blending them produces a house method that cites nobody. Its own graph kind rather than skills, for three properties a skill does not have: extractable (somebody else's work, adopted, so it lifts out with its declaration when the field moves on), referenced rather than inlined (two skills quoting one method is two copies free to drift), and exempt from skill criteria (skill-is-brief caps an INSTRUCTION near 280 lines; a methodology is a faithful rendering of an external standard, and truncating it to fit a house limit would misrepresent the standard). GRADE is deliberately NOT here — see smart-kg-methodologies.

Everything a QA process produced, in one declared tree. The owner's rule, 2026-09-19: an artefact generated primarily as a QA reviewer belongs under `test/results/` as part of a QA process — placement follows PROVENANCE, not file family and not who fetches it afterwards. Three kinds live here and the FILES say which they are, per the `$schema` contract: `qa-results/v1` (`<producer>.qa-results.json`, a whole-artefact review — findings about a document the build just produced), `qa-witness/v1` (`witnesses/**`, one per audited subject in the families `block`, `kg` and `translation`, the published projection) and `kg-qa/v1` (`kg-qa/**`, the KG verdicts themselves — what `kg-audit` wrote). The `kg-qa/` tree MIRRORS each subject's path rather than being flat, and that is not tidiness: measured 2026-09-19, four sidecar basenames already occur twice across packages (`editor`, `getting-started`, `idle-backlog`, `l2-dak-authoring`), so a flat directory would silently overwrite four verdicts. `kgQaSidecarPath` in `schemas/kg-qa.ts` is the one answer for writer and reader alike. A directory is a PLACE TO LOOK and may hold more than one part of a graph; extension is a coincidence, a declaration inside the file is the contract. ONE entry rather than a nested set, deliberately: #263's own comment names the defect a declaration inside another declaration creates. STILL OUTSIDE: the 122 block verdicts `*.qa.json`, which sit beside their blocks and move next. The witnesses are PUBLISHED at `/assets/qa/`, which is where every badge points; the publishing workflows copy them into `_site/assets/qa/` after Jekyll, since Jekyll builds only `docs/`. Where a file lives and where it is served from are different questions.

The trashcan that is kept. Deprecated and throwaway structured content — addressable, exported as <base>/fsh-guts.jsonld, and DELIBERATELY absent from the rendered site. Every other declared kind here is non-renderable because it is a graph a tool reads and there was never a page to make of it; this one's contents could be rendered and are not, so that something can be kept without being published. It is also the destination that makes the never-delete rule enforceable beyond beans: AGENTS.md forbids deleting a bean because a scrapped item stops the next agent re-entering a dead end while a deleted one cannot be told from an accident, and that reasoning was always general — an agent removing a page or a script had only `rm`. Delete now means relocate here, and relocate is reversible. Files declare themselves with `$schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1`, per the same contract the bean and workflow stores use. NOTE on the name: `.fsh` is FHIR Shorthand in this codebase and across the WHO SMART folios; the collision was raised and the owner confirmed this spelling. REPOSITORY-scoped: it sits at the top of the checkout, not inside this instance, and it is deliberately never overlaid by a dependency.

Repository health reports — what the daily sweep under `test/health/` wrote. One `health-report/v1` document, declaring itself with a `$schema` tag rather than being duck-typed by path: a directory is a PLACE TO LOOK and the files inside say what they are. A SEPARATE graph from `qa`, and the line between them is about the SUBJECT, not the producer: a QA verdict judges an artefact this repository produced, against criteria that artefact is supposed to meet; a health report judges the REPOSITORY ITSELF — how big it has grown, how much of the publish branch the review previews occupy, whether the work plan has duplicates in it. Folding it into `qa` would leave a consumer asking for verdicts about this instance's content holding a fact about its clone. NOTE the path: it was `tests/health/results/` when this graph landed in #395, because this repository then had BOTH `test/` (the `qa` graph) and `tests/` (the Playwright e2e specs), and the owner asked for `tests/health`. #395 flagged that inconsistency in `skills/folio-core/directory-conventions.md` rather than resolving it, since relocating a declared directory as a side effect of adding a check is the `dh4f` shape, where a consumer scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. The owner settled it on `test/` the same day and it moved as its own change — bean `auap`, PR #400. The `id` here is unchanged, deliberately: an inheriting instance overrides on the entry's id and never on its path, so `health` still binds after the relocation. The e2e specs came to the declaration rather than the declaration to the specs, because `testDir` is one line of one config file and a declared path is what every downstream override resolves against.

The work plan. `beans/beans.json` declares its nodes — `defs` (work items) and `workflows` (running BPMN instance state). REPOSITORY-scoped: it sits at the top of the checkout, not inside this instance, and it is deliberately never overlaid by a dependency.

A PERSON's outstanding items — the human half of memory, as against `beans/`, which is the agent's workflow management. Not a second work plan: the two sit in different quadrants of one 2x2 (memory vs workflow management, human vs agent), and human workflow management is EMPTY, deliberately. `todos/todos.json` declares its nodes — `items` (raised about anything) and `feedback` (raised against a specific block, carrying the submitter's identity) — the same shape as `beans/beans.json`. REPOSITORY-scoped: it sits at the top of the checkout, not inside this instance, and it is deliberately never overlaid by a dependency.

Agent memory — durable facts an agent carries between sessions, one `"$schema": "folio-memory/v1"` node each, assembled into `.claude/agent-memory/<agent>/MEMORY.md`. `context` by the axis bean `mhh9` settled: read during a process, never written by one; it changes when a human directs an authoring agent. It sat in `skills/memory/` until 2026-09-20 — inside the `cat-harness` directory, which is `content` — so the CONTAINING kind and the contents were on opposite layers, and a nested declaration is the defect #263 names. Moving it was held back from the classification change on purpose (#395's rule, and bean `auap`'s precedent: a relocation is its own change) and is bean `07xs`. SCOPE IS `repository`, like `beans/`: these are facts about this REPOSITORY carried by the agents working in it, and `.claude/agents/` — the consumers — sit at the repository root too.

How a PERSON wants to be asked — committed, read at session start by every agent. `context` by the same test as agent memory: read during a process, never written by one, changed when a person states a preference. It sat in `.harness/`, undeclared, until 2026-09-20, which this repository's own dot-prefix guard forbids: a dot-prefixed directory is absent from a plain `ls`, from most file browsers and from a forge's web tree, and the file read at the start of every session was in the one place the conventions reject. The path is also `harness.config.json`'s `interaction` key, which defaults here — the declaration and the config now name the same place instead of one of them being a literal nobody checks. SCOPE IS `repository`, and omitting it was a live defect for an hour on 2026-09-20: without it the path resolves against the INSTANCE, so a consumer looked in `cat-harness/` while the content sat at the repository root — and `harness:dirs` then created the empty instance-level directory to satisfy the declaration, turning declared-but-absent into declared-and-empty, which is the `dh4f` false pass wearing a tidier face. Repository, not instance, for the same reason `beans/` and `todos/` are: these are read by every agent working in this repository, not by this instance's code.

How far an agent has read an issue: `lastCommentId`, `lastUpdatedAt` and `checkedAt`, one file per issue. NOT the comments — the marks say what was seen, and one of the two files here says so in its own note. Two marks rather than one because a comment EDITED after being read keeps its id, so the id alone would call it seen and an edited requirement is a changed requirement (`issue-working`). `state`: a running process writes one each time it checks. Moved out of `.harness/issue-comments/` on 2026-09-20 for the reason `.beans/` and `.harness/workflow/` moved on 2026-09-18 — the artefacts a person looks for first were the hardest to find. SCOPE IS `repository`, and omitting it was a live defect for an hour on 2026-09-20: without it the path resolves against the INSTANCE, so a consumer looked in `cat-harness/` while the content sat at the repository root — and `harness:dirs` then created the empty instance-level directory to satisfy the declaration, turning declared-but-absent into declared-and-empty, which is the `dh4f` false pass wearing a tidier face. Repository, not instance, for the same reason `beans/` and `todos/` are: these are read by every agent working in this repository, not by this instance's code.

The incoming queue of the document-ingestion pipeline — raw files as dropped, before ingestion. NOT L1 and NOT greppable as corpus: the corpus checklist searches library/ only, so a source still sitting here reads as absent to every consumer while the file is on disk. That is why it is a separate declaration from library/ rather than the same directory under two names.

L1 source content — one <bib-slug>/ per ingested document, holding sections/*.md, structure.json and, where the source was scanned, ocr/page-NNN.txt. Every knowledge-graph reference to a source resolves THROUGH here, never to a loose path or a bare URL.

Editorial voice profiles — named rule sets overlaid on the base house voice, one JSON per voice. A voice is a THIRD axis beside adapters (which partition block kinds) and profiles (which partition what a folio may contain): it partitions how prose reads. Opt-in: this instance ships four and activates none, because folio-assistant's own documentation carries no voice (issue #208).

The gettext side of translation — one directory per target locale holding `.pot` templates, `.po` catalogues and the `TranslationNode` `.ts` manifests that make each pair addressable in the graph. The INPUT to injection. There is deliberately NO matching declaration for the rendered OUTPUT: a translated page is the same kind of thing as the page it translates — renderable content, differing by a field — and it declares its own `lang` and `translation_source` in front matter, so the locale subtrees under `docs/` are DISCOVERED from the files rather than enumerated here. A first draft of PR #351 enumerated them, ten entries for five locales across two subtrees, and that restated what all ten files already said. Undeclared until 2026-09-19: the `dh4f` defect in reverse, five committed directories that no declaration mentioned.

A SECOND knowledge-graph directory, holding skills DIRECTLY rather than in package subdirectories: `src/skills/corpus-grep.md` sits beside the `corpus-grep.ts` that implements it, because a skill whose whole body is 'run this tool' belongs next to the tool. Undeclared until 2026-09-19 (bean `osbo`), which is the `dh4f` defect in reverse — committed graph content that no declaration mentioned, so every declaration-driven consumer scanned past it and `LOCAL_PACKAGES` carried a hand-written exception for the one package discovery could not see. The id is NOT `cat-harness`: overrides match on id, and `skills/` already holds that one, so reusing it would replace the graph rather than add to it.

Authored content of this instance itself, rendered to a website. Holds the landing sticky — the instance's own description and its onboarding links, as a page-global note rather than text composited into the backdrop.

GRADE, and the first content in smart-kg. Certainty-of-evidence grading belongs to WHO L1 guideline development rather than to an agent framework: a folio formalising mathematics has evidence and no use for GRADE. Separated so the extraction is literal — smart-kg/ lifts out whole — which is the layout #223 asks for and bootstrap/ already demonstrates, and it is why this path is repository-scoped, like the bootstrap entry, rather than instance-relative. It has a slot waiting rather than needing one built: evidence-retrieval.bpmn runs Task_AppraiseGrade against "the grading system the folio declares", and its own documentation calls that a STRAWPERSON. Adopting the method as a sub-graph keeps the slot pluggable instead of wiring one system into the diagram.
